title: Horace Eubanks
summary: Garland thinks he knew Horace Eubanks in Chicago, and the interviewer discusses what little is known of him.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Did you ever know Horace Eubanks? I've been trying to find out about him for years.
Where did you know him, though?
I've known Horace. I think in Chicago.

Mm-hmm. I know he recorded with Charlie Roll Morton up there in Chicago, so I figured he's got to have been around there. Oh, and he played on the riverboat with Willie Humphrey in Dewey Jackson's band, too.
He played here. I was Fountain Blue. He played here on the boat.
He played here, didn't he, on the boat?
He might have. I never have heard about it, though. Because that's a mysterious man to me, Horace Eubanks. You know, I just never knew much about it.
